description: The Coastal Flood Exposure Mapper is an online visualisation tool that helps communities assess coastal hazard risks and vulnerabilities. It builds user-defined maps of the people, places and natural resources exposed to coastal flooding, which can be saved, downloaded or shared, with guidance on using the maps to engage stakeholders. Its coverage is the coastal contiguous United States, Hawaii and the territories. The map services and a document describing the underlying data are published alongside the tool, which is maintained by NOAA's Office for Coastal Management. Access is free and public; no licence is stated beyond US government data. Caveats: exposure layers combine flood hazard zones, sea level rise scenarios and census data at different resolutions, and the maps are screening tools, not site assessments. It supports hazard exposure analysis of critical facilities, infrastructure and population in coastal flood and sea level rise scenarios; a related record is the NOAA Digital Coast critical facilities dataset.
